newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Cano Limon pipeline reopens after blast.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Cano Limon pipeline reopens after blast.

text.p: Pumping restarted Thursday morning along Colombia's main oil pipeline after leftist rebels dynamited it three times in a week, a spokesman for the state oil company Ecopetrol said.

Crude is initially being sent to the country's two main oil refineries at the oil production center of Barrancabermeja and the Caribbean coast facility at Cartagena, which handle a combined total of about 280,000 barrels per day.
But the Ecopetrol spokesman said two tankers, in dock at the lifting terminal of Covenas, also on the Caribbean coast, would begin loading Thursday afternoon.
The cargoes, one of 460,000 barrels and the other of 390,000 barrels, are bound Peru and the United States, industry sources say. The Ecopetrol spokesman was unable to confirm this.
The pipeline, which runs from the Cano Limon field operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp in eastern Colombia to Covenas has been blasted 34 times this year by leftist rebels.
The Ecopetrol spokesmen said estimates were not yet available on the cost of repairs nor of how much crude had been spilled in the latest attacks on June 11, 15 and 17.
The attacks were blamed on the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest rebel force which frequently targets oil infrastructure.

In the year's other 31 attacks, more than 99,000 barrels of crude were spilled. Last year the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline was blown up 47 times with the loss of 105,000 barrels of crude. The cost of the environmental clean-up, repairs and the value of lost crude was put at about $9.3 million.
